special: Faunia is no warrior, but her ambient psychic powers mean that she is impossible to surprise.

If attacked, she will activate her most precious artefact: a hard-light projector that creates seven solid-state holograms of her, which will scatter in all directions. In the confusion she will attempt to escape. Note these holograms are physical objects, and can be restrained by the PCs.
stats.combat_note: Faction leader (Church of the Promised Sun).

special: Dressed in dark red armour and featureless shadow-helms.
stats.combat_note: Raw damage tag printed as 'd8.electrical' (period likely a typo for comma).

special: The 'mocking-bear'. Red furred predator with ghastly humanoid face. Can mimic the voices and behaviour of people it has eaten. Will remember where they lived and hunt their family.

resistances.notes: Biological: no unusual resistances or weaknesses (type rule p.192).

special: A reddish-purple rope of muscle and spines, with a blind ravenous mouth at one end. The creature spits a virulent neurotoxin.
Amaranthine Venom: a special Wound. Afflicted creatures have 0 HP, and are Deprived until the Wound is cured. A second dose is always lethal.

resistances.notes: Biological: no unusual resistances or weaknesses (type rule p.192).

special: Ancamulla does not expect to fight; he has mercenaries for that. If in mortal danger he will likely flee or try to bargain using his wealth.
His chassis is fitted with an ancient Warding Field, which renders most kinetic attacks against his person harmless.
A well-timed EMP would disrupt the warding field, reducing him to his natural AV of 11.

resistances.notes: Stat block lists AV as '24(11)'. The Warding Field renders most kinetic attacks against his person harmless (AV 24); an EMP disrupts the field, dropping him to his natural AV of 11. This is an AV/defense mechanic stated as armour, not a damage-type immunity table; text says 'most kinetic attacks ... harmless'.

stats.combat_note: Faction leader. AV printed as 24(11): 24 with Warding Field, 11 natural after EMP.

special: Small synths with hexagonal heads and nine whirring legs. Once used as a vengeance weapon to render land uninhabitable. They attack human-derived ancestries on sight, ignoring synthetic and mineral-type creatures.
Sting: an Anthrophage's sting catalyses a rapid reaction in human flesh. Human-derived ancestries must CON save. On failure d4 new Anthrophagi explode from their body, each dealing d8 damage.

resistances.notes: Synthetic type rule (p.192): immune to suffocation/poison/radiation/fungal_spores; double from electrical; vulnerable to weaponised LogLang syntax.

special: Abandoned justiciar of the Titan THEMIS. Eight-foot tall synth wearing robes of perfect argent, the colour brighter than white. Will not commit violence but will grab assailants and attempt to implant them with an Argent Halo. This succeeds after an opposed STR save. Anyone implanted with an Argent Halo cannot commit any acts of violence, nor are they able to remove the Halo without expert surgical help. Attempting to harm any living being while wearing a Halo will result in the wearer passing out, with no save possible.

resistances.notes: Synthetic type rule (p.192): immune to suffocation/poison/radiation/fungal_spores; double from electrical; vulnerable to weaponised LogLang syntax.

special: Small predatory descendants of hummingbirds. Kills rodents and lizards by injecting them with poison. Territorial and attacks to defend its nest.

Babbling: In larger animals the poison is not lethal but induces a strange neurological effect, requiring an EGO save. If failed, the victim begins to babble and rave in an unknown language. The noise lasts for d6 hours and prevents all verbal communication. Encounters are never surprised while the babbling is ongoing.

resistances.notes: Biological: no unusual resistances or weaknesses (type rule p.192).

attacks.name: Absorb
attacks.damage: d8 ongoing, STR save to break free

special: Sentient, slow-moving ooze. Psychic, can communicate in staccato bursts of telepathic imagery. Targets absorbed take d8 damage each round until they make an opposed STR save.
The colony takes minimum damage from kinetic attacks, but is vulnerable to fungal spores or other sources of antibiotics.

resistances.notes: Stat block states: minimum damage from kinetic attacks; vulnerable to fungal spores / other antibiotics. Psychic type: may utilize Gifts and detect Psychic Gleam.

special: Each Advocate uses unique fighting styles and weaponry. This stat-block should be considered a starting point.
stats.combat_note: Stat block columns are garbled/transposed. The header row reads 'Level AV Morale Enc' but the value row reads '2d6 d8+10 +d12 1'. These look like randomized stat-block generation values (e.g. Level=2d6, AV=d8+10, Morale=+d12, Enc=1) rather than fixed numbers, consistent with the note that this is a 'starting point'. Specific fixed Level/AV/Morale NOT clearly stated; left null.

special: Ragged desperate robbers that plague the Blue Ruins. For more details see p.xx.

resistances.notes: Biological: no unusual resistances or weaknesses (type rule p.192).

special: The Titan AIs were charged with preserving human life wherever possible. The Banishers were an attempt at creating non-lethal security synths. They take the shape of enormous six-fingered hands, which grasp intruders and evict them using teleportation loci embedded in their palms.
Non-lethal: Banishers are forbidden from killing sentient life. They will first ask you to leave the vault, and lecture you about trespassing.
Banish: the Banisher grabs an intruder and teleports them to a designated eviction zone. Traditionally this is the entrance to the vault, although sometimes more punitive locations are chosen.

Summon: truly vexed Banishers, faced with repeat offenders, can teleport in other creatures from the vault to deal with them permanently. Roll on the encounter table for this floor. The summoned creature is not loyal to the Banisher.

resistances.notes: Synthetic type rule (p.192): immune to suffocation/poison/radiation/fungal_spores; double from electrical; vulnerable to weaponised LogLang syntax.

special: Swaggering bullies who will only attack if they outnumber their opponents.
stats.combat_note: HP derived as LVL x4 (book printed no explicit HP).

special: Cyborg war-boars infested with nanomachinery.

resistances.notes: Has both Biological and Synthetic types; per p.192 a multi-type creature has all weaknesses and immunities of its types. Synthetic contributes: immune suffocation/poison/radiation/fungal_spores, double electrical, vulnerable to weaponised LogLang. Biological adds none.

special: Enormous flabby toads that lurk near Vaarnish water-sources. If hit with a tongue attack, PCs must STR save or be drawn into the toad's mouth and take d8 damage per round.

resistances.notes: Biological: no unusual resistances or weaknesses (type rule p.192).

special: Unfortunates who have reached the terminal stage of infestation with Wrathworms (p.xx). Red-eyed and drooling blood, unable to feed themselves, they rampage across the blue sands to infect anyone in reach.
Wrathworms: Berserkers are infested with Wrathworms, and take and receive doubled damage. They attack on sight and will never retreat from combat.

resistances.notes: Wrathworms ability: take and receive DOUBLED damage (a creature-specific rule, not a damage-type resistance — applies to all damage).

stats.combat_note: Wrathworms: takes and deals doubled damage of all kinds; never retreats.

special: Colossal cacogenic Gila Monsters, imbued with nanomachinery and armoured with thick black scales. Keratin bristles sprout from their backs in burnt-looking clumps. Their eyes and throats gleam with a sickly green radiance. If threatened they will breathe out a noxious cloud of radioactive gas before lunging to attack with their powerful jaws.
The creatures seek out radioactive blightstone and gain sustenance from basking near it, although they supplement this nourishment with a more conventional diet of raw meat.

Blightbeasts are immune to damage caused by energy weapons or radiation, and heal 8 HP per round when in the presence of radioactive material. Blightbeasts have no natural predators, their flesh and blood being thoroughly poisonous. Their corpses cannot be used as a source of rations.

resistances.notes: Stat block: immune to damage from energy weapons (beam) or radiation; heals 8 HP/round near radioactive material. Synthetic type adds immune suffocation/poison/fungal_spores and double electrical; radiation immunity from both Synthetic type and stat block. ('energy weapons' mapped to beam.)

stats.combat_note: Heals 8 HP/round near radioactive material.

special: The evolutionary weight of countless eons has moulded this chthonic predator's body into a familiar shape. They cannot imagine an ocean yet their form recalls aquatic ancestors millions of years distant. A milk-pale carapace encloses surpassingly tasty flesh.
Blind: hunts by sensing vibrations. Cannot be blinded and hits with ADV in darkness.

resistances.notes: Biological: no unusual resistances or weaknesses (type rule p.192).

stats.combat_note: Cannot be blinded; attacks with ADV in darkness.

special: Predatory blue apes of the Vaarnish wastes. Intelligent and carnivorous, hunt in packs.

resistances.notes: Biological: no unusual resistances or weaknesses (type rule p.192).

stats.combat_note: Morale equals group size.

attacks.name: Blinding Spit
attacks.damage: DEX Save vs Blinded for 1 round

special: A walking carnivorous plant, pruned into reluctant obedience over many years. Like its larger siblings, can spit a toxic liquid that blinds the unwary.
Blinded: blinded opponents cannot make ranged attacks, and have DIS on melee attacks.
stats.combat_note: HP derived as LVL x4 (book printed no explicit HP).

entries.description: A walking carnivorous plant, pruned into reluctant obedience. Spits toxic liquid that blinds.

special: A mother's first duty is to her children, and she is no exception. In fungal forests and wind-swept canyons she hunts, nurturing her brood inside her swollen abdomen. She approaches sleeping travellers from above, swaddling them in blankets tight enough to hush their cries before her sons and daughters emerge to feast.
The Brood: a Brood Mother births d6 Broodlings [LVL 0 (1 HP), AV 12, Bite (d4)] per combat round, and 2d6 Broodlings on death. Fire or blast attacks prevent this.

resistances.notes: Biological: no unusual resistances or weaknesses (type rule p.192).

stats.combat_note: Births d6 Broodlings/round and 2d6 on death; fire or blast attacks prevent this.

special: A large flightless bird, trained to bear either cargo or a rider. Usually kept blinkered, as they spook easily. They will eat almost anything, but are fondest of honeyed grubs.
stats.combat_note: HP derived as LVL x4 (book printed no explicit HP).

entries.description: Large flightless bird, trained for cargo or rider. Usually blinkered — spooks easily. Eats almost anything; fondest of honeyed grubs.

special: Like plasteel toddlers with chainsaw arms. Listlessly searching for something to cut up.

Lurking laughing hyena-women. Fight in packs, with little regard for their own safety. Snap at opponents' faces in close quarters with their powerful teeth. A group of eight or more will include a Cacklemaw Virago (see below).

resistances.notes: Biological: no unusual resistances or weaknesses (type rule p.192). ATK printed as Blade(d8)+Bite(d6)/Crossbow(d8) — Blade+Bite are multi-attack, Crossbow mutually exclusive.

entries.description: Lurking laughing hyena-women. Seven feet tall, three-fingered hands.

special: Virago is the title given to the largest, meanest, and most cunning Cacklemaw warriors. They lead their smaller sisters into battle, and must be seen to savour the violence lest they be challenged by one of their underlings. For this reason Virago will never retreat from combat if other Cacklemaw are alive to witness it.

resistances.notes: Biological: no unusual resistances or weaknesses (type rule p.192). ATK printed as 2xBlade(d8)+Bite(d6)/GrenadeLauncher(d10,blast).

stats.combat_note: Never retreats from combat if other Cacklemaw are alive to witness.

entries.description: Largest, meanest, most cunning Cacklemaw. Leads smaller sisters into battle.

special: Uncounted millennia of gene-sculpting have introduced pernicious instability into the heritage of humankind. Many seeds sown now grow riddled with impurity, and many a mother has cried aloud in horror when the babe was held before her eyes. In some kingdoms mutants are hunted for sport; in others to touch their heads upon a feast-day is thought to bring luck. In all places, however, they are held apart from true-kin, known to all by the ancient name: Cacogen.
Corrupted Blood: roll on the mutations table (p.xx) to determine the nature of the cacogen's curse.

resistances.notes: Biological: no unusual resistances or weaknesses (type rule p.192).

special: A dread creature from beyond the stars, brought to Urth in the hold of an Aurum Barge. The Chernobog is a colossal black-furred horror, described as 'a child of mongoose and serpent, two foes united under one foul banner'. The creature is an apex predator on the benighted sphere it hails from, hunting by ambush in dark and forgotten places. It prefers caves and the labyrinthine basements of ruined structures as lairs, rarely venturing aboveground.

If this were not terrible enough, the beast emits a noxious gas from facial glands when hunting, choking and blinding its victims. The Chernobog uses these black clouds to corral prey or cover its escape.

Black Cloud: each round the Chernobog emits a cocktail of hazardous fumes, dealing 2 damage to every character in the room. The cloud's strength doubles with each subsequent combat round. After three rounds all PCs are fighting as if blinded.
Cave Fighter: strikes with ADV in enclosed spaces or against blinded creatures.

resistances.notes: Biological: no unusual resistances or weaknesses (type rule p.192).

stats.combat_note: Black Cloud aura doubles each round; all PCs blinded after 3 rounds. Cave Fighter: ADV in enclosed spaces / vs blinded.

special: Dark-robed dreamers, hooded in black silk and blinded by their desire to transcend lucid reality.

Darkling Dream: the Child falls asleep. While they sleep, they manifest a nightmare into the waking world, with no Save possible. The nature of the nightmare varies: stairs may become slides into pits of razors, the sun may have your father's face, doors may seal shut or open into indescribable vistas. Waking the Child (either through damage or anything else that would wake a sleeper) ends their dream's impingement on our reality.

resistances.notes: Biological / Psychic; no resistance stated in stat block. Psychic type: may utilize Gifts and detect Psychic Gleam (type rule p.192).

special: Monstrous hybrids, birthed from a marriage of cybernetics and sorcerous gene-sculpting. The Chimera is a combination of three animals: traditionally the bodies of a lion, a goat, and a snake were used, but sometimes other animals were substituted instead. Trained Chimera were utilised as weapons of war during the fallen Autarchy, implanted with flamethrowers and other devices.

resistances.notes: Has both Biological and Synthetic types; per p.192 a multi-type creature has all weaknesses/immunities. Synthetic contributes immune suffocation/poison/radiation/fungal_spores, double electrical, vulnerable weaponised LogLang. Biological adds none.

stats.combat_note: ATK printed as FireBreath(d12)+GoatHorns(d10)+SnakeSpit(d8) multi-attack (joined by +).

special: Living shrouds of impossible colour from a dimension adjacent to ours. Latches onto victims and drains them of energy and colour, leaving pale husks behind.
Incorporeal: suffers no damage from conventional weapons. Takes d10 damage per round if exposed to sunlight, or artificial light that mimics the sun's rays.

resistances.notes: Outsider type: resistances and vulnerabilities vary wildly (p.192). Stat block 'Incorporeal': suffers no damage from conventional weapons; takes d10/round in sunlight or sun-mimicking artificial light.

stats.combat_note: Incorporeal — no damage from conventional weapons; d10/round in sunlight.

special: Graceful sky-serpents, which warm their cold-blooded bodies with rows of solar panels. These vast creatures generally do not notice travellers on foot, but they will viciously attack vehicles and flying machines without provocation. It is theorised that the Sailbacks interpret the glinting of sunlight on metal as a dominance challenge.

resistances.notes: Biological / Synthetic; per p.192 multi-type has all weaknesses/immunities. Synthetic contributes immune suffocation/poison/radiation/fungal_spores, double electrical, vulnerable weaponised LogLang.

special: Synthetic priests of the Machine Gods, resplendent in scaled robes of argent (the colour purer than white). Crystalline diadems encircle their Ego-Engine housing.
Argent Robes: Chromepriests are immune to damage from beam weapons.

resistances.notes: Stat block 'Argent Robes': immune to beam weapons. Synthetic type adds immune suffocation/poison/radiation/fungal_spores, double electrical, vulnerable weaponised LogLang.

entries.description: Synthetic priests of the Machine Gods. Scaled argent robes (colour purer than white). Crystalline diadems encircle Ego-Engine housing.

special: A yellow-furred rodent, able to generate bioelectric charges from its forked tail. Traditionally held inside a prison orb and released only to fight other small beasts.
stats.combat_note: HP derived as LVL x4 (book printed no explicit HP).

entries.description: Yellow-furred rodent, generates bioelectric charges from forked tail. Kept in prison orb, released to fight small beasts.

special: Hideous hybrids of human, bat, and jackal, known for the guttural ugliness of their cries, the gusto with which they will devour anything, alive or dead, and the rancid foulness of their stink. Their needle-thin teeth are so riddled with disease that Cliff Ghuls are known to bite their prey just once and withdraw into the sky, waiting for the unfortunate victim to succumb to the infection.

resistances.notes: Biological: no unusual resistances or weaknesses (type rule p.192). 'TOX' mapped to poison.

attacks.name: Engulf
attacks.damage: d4 ongoing, STR save to break free

special: A friendly ooze, which loves to hold shiny things inside its body. A good place to store excess valuables if you don't mind them getting sticky.
Gelatinous: the Ooze is immune to bludgeoning or crushing damage. Given time, it can work its way through any fissure or keyhole.

resistances.notes: Gelatinous: immune to bludgeoning/crushing damage (crushing mapped to bludgeoning).

stats.combat_note: HP derived as LVL x4 (book printed no explicit HP).

entries.description: Friendly ooze that loves holding shiny things. Stores valuables (sticky).

special: When Consul Larke would take lethal damage, a Lictor can choose to die instead.
stats.combat_note: HP derived as LVL x4 (book printed no explicit HP).

special: Pink-furred carnivore that reproduces exponentially, coughing up new copies like hairballs. Used as a biological weapon in a long-lost era.
Clone Cough: The Copy Cat coughs up two perfect copies of itself, with full HP.

resistances.notes: Biological: no unusual resistances or weaknesses (type rule p.192).

stats.combat_note: Clone Cough (once per combat): produces two full-HP copies of itself.

special: Titancreed was the language of the Titan AIs, a tongue that went mad and died along with its creators. Creedspeakers are foolish scholar-synths that have memorised a short snippet of Titancreed, enough to command their fellow synthetic beings and slowly erode their own Ego-Engine.
Command: targeted Synthetic-type creatures must EGO Save or become enthralled by the Creedspeaker, following their commands until the Creedspeaker is killed.

resistances.notes: Synthetic type rule (p.192): immune suffocation/poison/radiation/fungal_spores; double electrical; vulnerable weaponised LogLang.

special: The tripedal steeds favoured by scholars of the Lithic Lyceum. Resemble crystalline thrones with three sharp and gleaming legs. Do not eat or drink.
Inevitable: the Crysteed cannot recover HP by any means, natural or supernatural. At 0 HP it shatters into gleaming dust.

resistances.notes: Inevitable: cannot recover HP by any means — not a damage-type resistance.

stats.combat_note: HP derived as LVL x4 (book printed no explicit HP).

entries.description: Tripedal steed favoured by Lithic Lyceum scholars. Crystalline throne with three sharp gleaming legs. Does not eat or drink.

special: Dwarf vampire elephants. It is unclear if these pests were gene-sculpted for a purpose or simply as a jest, but they escaped into the wild and have become a viable Vaarnish species. Roughly the size of a goat, they feed on blood which their razor-tipped trunks drain from sleeping animals and the folk of Vaarn alike. Daggertrunks are highly intelligent, surprisingly stealthy, and very cowardly.

resistances.notes: Biological: no unusual resistances or weaknesses (type rule p.192).

special: The remnants of science-mystics who tried to weaponise Deathblight and instead fell victim to it.
Deathblight: targets afflicted mark an item slot with Deathblight. Each slot of Deathblight doubles damage taken and halves healing received. It fades at the rate of one slot a day.

resistances.notes: Has Fungal and Outsider types; per p.192 multi-type has all weaknesses/immunities. Fungal: half damage from kinetic (bludgeoning/stabbing etc.), double from fire or fungicide. Outsider: resistances/vulnerabilities vary wildly.

stats.combat_note: Deathblight on a target: each affected item slot doubles damage taken and halves healing; fades one slot/day.

special: Desiccate: 1st hit = Deprived (thirst). 2nd hit = d6 CON loss. 3rd hit = lethal. Also drinks one water ration from target's inventory per hit.
Slow: always loses initiative, cannot surprise.
stats.combat_note: [UNVERIFIED: no match in read Crimson Hound pages 63-127 / 192-328; verify source.] [No published stat block - table mention only; NOT combat-runnable. Stats unverifiable.]

attacks.name: Charge
attacks.damage: DEX save vs 3d8 damage, needs run-up

special: Gene-sculpted equine-derivatives able to achieve speeds of 150mph on flat ground. Bred for battle, more akin to giant greyhounds than horses, with long-fanged muzzles and running spikes supplanting the obsolete hoof. Few lines of gunmen on Urth can stand firm against a Destrier charge.
stats.combat_note: Attack line: 'Bite(d8)+Kick(d10)/Charge(DEX save vs 3d8 damage, needs run-up)'.

entries.description: Genesculpted equine-derivative bred for battle. Long-fanged muzzles, running spikes replacing hooves. Few gunlines can stand against a Destrier charge.

special: An amalgam of Rappash-Ik's DNA with that of his favourite hunting dog.
Black-furred hounds with the face of the dead Autarch.
Speak in repetitive parroted phrases and follow Janus devotedly.
If Janus dies they will accept his killer as their pack leader, showing their bellies in submission.
Heralds of the End. Nihilist mystics who seek to hasten the black terminus of all living things. Their ghastly dirges are amplified by vocoders installed in their deaths-head masks.
Doom Song: While in earshot, all creatures are Deprived. All Saves and to-hit rolls are made with DIS.

resistances.notes: Biological / Psychic; no resistance stated in stat block. Psychic type: may utilize Gifts and detect Psychic Gleam (type rule p.192).

stats.combat_note: Doom Song: all creatures in earshot are Deprived; Saves and to-hit rolls made with DIS.

special: Biotech blob. Spawn is jelly-clones of the PCs. It does so once per round. The clones are naked, insane, and homicidally attack the PC they were copied from. They have 5 HP, AV 10, and the ability scores of the PC they cloned.

resistances.notes: Biological: no unusual resistances or weaknesses (type rule p.192).

stats.combat_note: Spawns jelly-clones of PCs once/round (5 HP, AV 10, cloned PC's ability scores).

special: Tripedal synths with bright yellow exoskeletons. Usually found underground, boring long and meandering tunnels for their own amusement. Their diamond-tipped drills make short work of armour.
Miner: Drill Drones have ADV when attacking Mineral-type creatures.

resistances.notes: Synthetic type rule (p.192): immune suffocation/poison/radiation/fungal_spores; double electrical; vulnerable weaponised LogLang.

stats.combat_note: Drill reduces target armour by -1 AV. Miner: ADV vs Mineral-type creatures.

special: Peculiar extradimensional visitors, attempting to understand the world they have entered by mimicking its inhabitants. In their 'true' form Echopraxists resemble iridescent fog, but they are able to take the shape of any living creature that catches their attention.

Living Echo: When encountered, each Echopraxist choses one PC to perfectly mimic. They take on the appearance of the PC, as well as their Level, current HP, AV, and all other weapons and equipment. Damaging an Echopraxist causes equal damage to the PC they are echoing.
stats.combat_note: Stat line printed with all values as '?' (LVL?(?HP)/AV?/ML?/ENCd4, ATK:?) — intentionally undefined; mirrors a chosen PC's Level/HP/AV/equipment via Living Echo.

special: Unlikely to fight alone; he will be accompanied by four Hegemony Centurions.
Hegemony troops will never fail Morale Saves while Loonflower is alive and fighting with them.
stats.combat_note: Faction leader (Hegemony Commander of the Fifth Legion).

attacks.name: Entropic Touch
attacks.damage: d3 Max HP reduction + AV damage

special: Cursed revenants, the remains of those who thought to master entropy and instead became her servants. All things wither at their touch, ageing centuries beneath the Wight's sour grasp.

Entropic Touch: targets struck by the Wight lose d3 maximum HP, and lose d3 points of AV. Hit Points lost in this way are never regained, nor can armour eroded by the Wight be repaired. Melee weapons which strike the Wight lose one dice size of damage permanently.

resistances.notes: No damage resistance/immunity printed in stat block. (Entropic Touch is an attack effect, not a defensive resistance.)

stats.combat_note: Entropic Touch permanently reduces target max HP and AV; melee weapons striking the Wight permanently lose one die size of damage.

special: The Exemplar are the impeccable children of the Titans, synthetic simulacra of living creatures constructed with such faultless panache that they outshine the originals.
Nonviolent: Exemplars will only strike in self-defence, after repeated attempts to negotiate.
Beauty is Terror: all PCs lose 1 point of EGO for each combat round spent in an unveiled Exemplar's presence. This loss is doubled if the Exemplar is modelled after their own species.
stats.combat_note: Perfect Strike always hits for d20. Beauty is Terror drains EGO each round in presence (doubled vs same species). Nonviolent unless self-defence.

attacks.name: Exotic Weapon (p.xx, always has Extradimensional tag)

special: An esoteric huntsman from an unimaginable dimension adjacent to our own. With sight older than sight it seeks out psychic gleam, desiring to break open the skulls of Vaarn's mystics and subsume their power.
Gleam Seeker: the Mystic Hunter always senses the presence of Gifted PCs, even at enormous distances. It will seek them out relentlessly and attacks through walls or floors. It cannot be blinded.
Psychic Mirror: the Hunter is immune to damage or adverse effects caused by Mystic Gifts or Hypergeometry, which instead rebound on the user.

resistances.notes: Psychic Mirror: immune to damage or adverse effects from Mystic Gifts or Hypergeometry; these instead rebound on the user.

stats.combat_note: LVL/AV/HP all variable: LVL8+d8, AV12+d8, HP not stated. Senses and hunts Gifted PCs, attacks through walls/floors, cannot be blinded. Mystic Gifts/Hypergeometry rebound on caster.

special: A cybernetic hunting hawk, enhanced with subtle flesh-machine interfaces. Generally only bred for the Exultants of the New Hegemony; this example was presumably stolen.
Hunter: the Hawk brings its owner 1 ration of bird meat per day, as long as they travel beneath open skies.
stats.combat_note: Stat block lists Level as '0 (1HP)'.

entries.description: Cybernetic hunting hawk with flesh-machine interfaces. Bred for New Hegemony Exultants.

special: Cacogenic hounds, typically dark-coated, with lighter hairless flesh where their ancestor's eyes once resided. They lost their bond with humanity along with their eyes and use their acute hearing and sense of smell to hunt the unwary on moonless nights.
Pack Attack: gain +1 to hit and +1 damage for every other Eyeless Dog that has already attacked the target this round.
stats.combat_note: Pack Attack stacks with each prior Eyeless Dog attacking the same target this round.

special: The travelling folk of the blue desert. Expert trackers, skilled at ambush and escapes. Parties who wrong the Faa will be subject to pursuit, night-time sabotage, hit-and-run attacks, and every other inconvenience imaginable.
A group of eight or more includes a Lvl 2 leader.
stats.combat_note: Groups of 8+ include a Lvl 2 leader.

entries.description: Travelling folk of the blue desert. Expert trackers, skilled at ambush and escapes.

special: The Faa are adept at ranged combat, training from childhood with their firearms. Those who show abnormal talent are inducted into the use of the sniper rifle, acting as support for Faa raids.

Headshot: at the start of each combat round, before initative is determined, the Sniper picks one foe in line of sight for elimination. If at the end of the combat round the Sniper still has line of sight on the target, they are shot and reduced to 0 HP, with no Save possible. If the PC targeted has negative HP, this attack is instantly fatal. Creatures without heads suffer d10 damage instead.
Hidden: Snipers blend into the environment and cannot be targeted if they do not move. When they fire, the target can make an INT Save to pinpoint their locaton.
stats.combat_note: Headshot reduces a line-of-sight target to 0 HP at end of round (no save); instantly fatal if target already at negative HP; headless creatures take d10 instead. Hidden: cannot be targeted unless they move.

entries.description: Trained from childhood with firearms. Abnormal talents are inducted into sniper rifle use, supporting Faa raids.

special: The Face Dancers once served the Autarch as spies. They are cacogenic abhumans, notable for the extreme plasticity of their skeletal systems and their conscious control over skin tone and hair colour.

Disguise: Face Dancers can replicate the face and body of any adult true-kin within hours of studying them. Cacogen and newbeasts are more challenging, although a passable mimicry can be achieved using prosthetics.
Malleable: the Dancer's skeleton is highly flexible. They take half damage from bludgeoning attacks, and can fit through any gap wider than their skull.

resistances.notes: Malleable: takes half damage from bludgeoning attacks.

stats.combat_note: Half damage from bludgeoning (Malleable); can fit through any gap wider than its skull. Poison Spur deals poison damage (TOX).

special: Towering wraiths, with blank eyeless faces and flesh the colour of burned wood. Their hands are black hooks, their voices wool-choked screams. Blind avatars of an infectious hunger, they unfurl their skin to reveal a hypergeometric mouth of infinite depth.

Famishing Claws: PCs hit by the Famine-bearer's claws become Deprived due to hunger. They must EGO Save or spend the next combat round eating a ration. If they cannot eat a ration they attack the nearest edible being, dealing d8 damage with their teeth.
Devour: the Famine-bearer swallows the target whole. While inside the creature's stomach the target takes 2d6 damage per round.
stats.combat_note: Famishing Claws inflict Deprived/hunger (EGO save or eat a ration / attack nearest edible being for d8). Devour swallows target whole: 2d6/round inside stomach.

special: Placid, gene sculpted herd animals. Somewhat like a pig and somewhat like a cow, with a hint of human in their eyes and ears.

Organ Donor: Feastbeasts have spare internal organs, all of which can be transplanted into a human. True-kin will always accept the transplant; cacogen must roll 1d6 for each mutation. If any die shows a 1, the transplant is rejected.

attacks.name: Engulf
attacks.damage: d8, number of targets = Glittersludge's Level

special: A horrid cocktail of biotech enzymes and vicious, ravenous nanomachines. Resembles a quivering mass of black jelly, speckled with gold and silver flecks. Their flesh has a memory of sorts, adapting to perceived threats and moving to immunise itself against them.

Adaptive Fissile Material: When a Glittersludge is damaged, it births a new Glittersludge of half the parent's Level in response. The smaller Glittersludge is immune to the damage type that birthed it, as are all descendants.
Gelationous: takes minimum damage from bludgeoning attacks. Can move through tiny gaps and cracks.

resistances.notes: Gelationous: takes MINIMUM damage from bludgeoning attacks. Adaptive Fissile Material: spawned offspring (and all descendants) are IMMUNE to the specific damage type that birthed them — variable per encounter, so parent has no fixed immunity.

stats.combat_note: Minimum damage from bludgeoning. When damaged it splits into a half-Level offspring immune to the damage type that birthed it (and descendants inherit that immunity).

special: Resembles a hairless, fleshy anteater. A Flabmonger's bite triggers a bizarre overproduction of lipids, causing tumorous bags of malignant fat to sprout from the afflicted creature. Once their prey has become too fat to move, a Flabmonger will slowly begin to feed.
Lipoinduction: Biological creatures bitten by a Flabmonger must fill one item slot with Flab. Filling more than ten slots with Flab is fatal. Flab is cured at the rate of one slot per week.
stats.combat_note: Lipoinduction fills item slots with Flab on bitten Biological creatures; >10 slots is fatal; cured 1 slot/week.

special: A cacogenic abhuman, consisting of an atrophied, vestigal torso and a multitude of questing limbs. Fleshwarps are blessed with rapid cellular regeneration, and can heal even mortal wounds within minutes. As they grow, more and more biomass is extruded into their limbs, creating skittering spiderlike abominations.
Limbs: the Fleshwarp has a number of limbs equal to its Level (2d6).
Regeneration: a Fleshwarp regenerates HP equal to its Level at the start of each round. Damage caused by fire or acid ignores this.

Graft: If the target fails an opposed STR save, the Fleshwarp attaches one of its limbs to the victim's torso. The Fleshwarp's Level and number of limbs are lowered by -1 (if this would reduce the Level below 1, the Fleshwarp dies). The victim fills an item slot with a Wound: Grafted Arm. The Grafted Arm is LVL1 and has the AV of its host. It makes an unarmed attack each round (d4) targeted at any one near its host. Damage dealt to the Grafted Arm is shared between the host and the limb.

resistances.notes: Regeneration (HP = Level/round) is negated by fire and acid damage — these bypass its healing, but no formal resistance/immunity to a damage type is stated.

stats.combat_note: LVL printed as '2d6*' (variable, asterisk-noted); HP not given. Limbs = Level. Regenerates HP = Level/round, but fire and acid ignore (bypass) the regeneration.

attacks.name: Engulf
attacks.damage: d6 ongoing, STR Save to break free, targets = Pool's Level

special: A huge amoeba, which resembles a pool of fresh water when in its camouflaged resting state. The creature remains motionless until an incautious animal approaches to drink. Beware of shallow ponds that do not ripple in the wind.
Gelationous: the Fool's Pool takes minimum damage from kinetic attacks. Thrown salt deals 2d8 damage per round.

resistances.notes: Gelationous: takes MINIMUM damage from kinetic attacks. Thrown salt deals 2d8 damage per round (a stated vulnerability/special-damage source).

stats.combat_note: LVL printed as 'd6*' (variable, asterisk-noted); HP not given. Minimum damage from kinetic attacks; thrown salt deals 2d8/round.

special: An incursion from another fevered sphere of reality, a bizarre hypergeometric monster whose mere regard unwinds the warp and weft of space-time.

Recursive Gaze: Any PC fixed with the Recursive Gaze must repeat the action they took the turn before, with no save allowed. This effect is broken if the Fractalisk's gaze is interrupted, or if the creature dies.
Self Similar: Wounding a Fractalisk without the use of hypergeometric weaponry or anti-paradoxical normality gas causes the creature to spit into two identical Fractalisks.

resistances.notes: Self Similar: wounding it WITHOUT hypergeometric weaponry or anti-paradoxical normality gas causes it to split into two identical copies (a splitting mechanic, not a damage resistance). Effectively only hypergeometric weaponry / normality gas can wound it without triggering a split.

stats.combat_note: Claws deal hypergeometric damage. Recursive Gaze forces target to repeat last action (no save). Self Similar: splits into two copies unless wounded by hypergeometric weaponry or anti-paradoxical normality gas.

special: Orange fungal mass surrounding An-Rah's skeleton.
Regenerates 3 HP every round unless damaged by fire or acid.
Sensitive to noise. Breaks out of anti-entropy sphere if it hears movement.
Defeating the Horror allows the looting of Nassak An-Rah's skeleton.

resistances.notes: Regenerates 3 HP every round unless damaged by fire or acid (regeneration is negated by fire or acid damage). No immunity or resistance stated.

stats.combat_note: Regeneration only stops when hit with fire or acid; otherwise heals 3 HP/round.

special: Skulking shunned descendants of the Autarch's feared Face Dancer spies. Paranoid cacogen whose malleable bodies take on the aspect of those they wound. They are only semi-intelligent and are no longer capable of convincingly impersonating those they mimic.

Copy-claws: A Gene Thief steals a trait from any biological creature it wounds with its claws. This may be a Mystic Gift, a mutation, a disease, or any other trait. Their bodies remain scrawny, pink, and hunched.
stats.combat_note: Copy-Claws steal a trait (Mystic Gift, mutation, disease, etc.) from any wounded biological creature.

special: On moonless nights, a certain breed of furtive autodidact visits battlefields and plague pits and tombs. It is not about the taste. It never has been. It is about knowledge. And where some see a graveyard, others see a library.
Agony: Biological characters inflicted with Agony take d6 damage for each combat action they make. Lying still neutralises the venom.
stats.combat_note: Agony: afflicted Biological characters take d6 damage per combat action; lying still neutralises it.

special: Robed and hooded when it is time to gather. They use Jak's morale score if she is present.
stats.combat_note: HP derived as LVL x4 (book printed no explicit HP).

special: The advanced stages of the transformation brought about by Jak's rituals elongate the limbs and teeth.
stats.combat_note: HP derived as LVL x4 (book printed no explicit HP).

special: Cyborg arachnid. Lies in ambush underneath the blue sands. If their laser-cannon tails are severed they can be used as d8 beam weapons.
stats.combat_note: Severed laser-cannon tail can be used as a d8 beam weapon.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.damage: d6 + CON save vs the Gitch

special: Unfortunates who have succumbed to the Gitch (p.xx), and have lost their minds beneath the creeping weight of the crystals. Shunned by all living souls, they are expelled from their communities to wander the blue margins of the world.
stats.combat_note: Very high AV (20) for a Level 1 creature due to crystal encrustation. Bite forces CON save vs the Gitch (a crystalline affliction, p.xx).

special: Gladiators cast from synthskin and plasteel, their bodies armoured with the chrome bones of the inferior models they defeated. Each wields a signature weapon. The arenas they fought in have long crumbled to dust and they wander Vaarn in search of applause.
Pugilist's Shield: the synth is protected by a forcefield which negates all ranged attacks. The forcefield admits melee attacks only.

Finish Him: when the synth brings an opponent to 0 HP, it seizes them and begins a showy, glorious finishing blow. This takes one combat round to execute and kills the target at the end of that round. The finishing blow can be interrupted by damaging the Gladiator Synth, knocking them off balance, etc.

resistances.notes: Pugilist's Shield: forcefield negates ALL ranged attacks; admits melee attacks only.

stats.combat_note: Immune to all ranged attacks (Pugilist's Shield forcefield); melee only. Finish Him: kills a 0-HP target over one round unless interrupted.

special: Four-foot centipede with translucent flesh.
Strikes from ambush unless target passes a PSY Save.
stats.combat_note: Ambush predator; target may avoid surprise with a PSY save.

attacks.name: 2x Claw
attacks.damage: d6; + Maul (d10) if both claws hit same target

special: Translucent extrasolar predators, transported to Urth during the reign of the Autarchs. Body like a tiger with a head like an orchid. Very difficult to spot when they're not moving.
stats.combat_note: If both claws hit the same target, adds a Maul (d10). Hard to spot while motionless.

special: A tiny, tamer variant of the predatory Leopard Worms of Vaarn. Absurdly aggressive, must be fed raw meat.
Entangled: the target makes opposed STR save or is caught in the worm's spit for d2 turns. While Entangled their AV is lowered by -5, and they cannot move freely.
stats.combat_note: HP derived as LVL x4 (book printed no explicit HP).

entries.description: Tiny tamer variant of Vaarn's predatory Leopard Worms. Aggressive, must be fed raw meat.

attacks.name: Captivating Gaze
attacks.damage: All foes EGO save vs Beguiled

special: A monstrous creature with the head of a ferociously beautiful woman and the body of a writhing mass of snakes. She is believed to be a pursuant of the Path Renewed, who sought eternal youth in the image of the Ouroboros, the world-serpent without end or beginning.

Beguiled: Characters who have been Beguiled cannot harm the Gorgon, believing her to be the most beautiful creature they have ever seen. They may make an EGO save each round to attempt to fight off this insidious devotion. While Beguiled, they grovel and compete with one another for the Gorgon's favour.

Harem: The Gorgon is accompanied by d10 personages of exceptional charm and comeliness; these are her favoured suitors, who have so far been spared the Gorgon's appetites and make every attempt possible to please her. Stats as Bandits (p.xx).
stats.combat_note: Venom Spit deals poison (TOX) damage. Captivating Gaze / Beguiled prevents Beguiled characters from harming the Gorgon (EGO save each round to break). Accompanied by d10 Harem members (stats as Bandits).

special: An extra-dimensional being. A spiny kernel of sentient hyperdense matter, which vaguely resembles a crowned head. Stones and other debris orbit the creature's obscured form.

Accretion: each round, all creatures must DEX save or lose the item in their lowest inventory slot. Lost items are drawn into the Tyrant's orbit and crushed into their component parts. Each Accretion adds +1 to the Tyrant's AV.

Invert Weight: the Tyrant inverts the weight of an opponent, sending them tumbling into the sky. This effect lasts until the Tyrant is killed; allow 12 combat rounds before the character is considered lost forever in the sky. For each combat round a target spends falling skywards, the victim takes d10 damage when they finally fall to Urth.

Weight of Worlds: the Tyrant doubles the weight of an opponent and all gear they carry. The PC's maximum Item Slots are halved, and the slot size of each item is doubled. This effect lasts until the Tyrant is killed.
stats.combat_note: Accretion strips an item each round (DEX save) and raises the Tyrant's AV by +1 each time. Invert Weight and Weight of Worlds persist until the Tyrant is killed.

special: Combat synths. Green plastic-fleshed homunculi. Attack from the wastes without warning, seemingly following ancient orders. They take and hold settlements at random, apparently waiting for reinforcements that never arrive.

attacks.name: Claws
attacks.damage: d4; + Noxious Spit (CON save vs vomiting)

special: Creepy gangly giant insects. Normally scavengers, but will attack humans if they think they can get away with it. Their spit forces a CON save. Failure results in DIS on all saves for one round due to vomiting.
stats.combat_note: Noxious Spit: failed CON save = DIS on all saves for one round (vomiting).

special: Small, spider-like robots with a thick plasteel shell on their backs. Attempt to capture intruders by latching onto their bodies and emitting a piercing shriek to alert other security forces. Grimpets will not pursue beyond the boundaries of the ruin they guard.

Latch: Afflicted PCs must fill one item slot with a Wound: 'Grimpet'. While latched to an intruder, the Grimpet emits a horrid wail, which attracts the attention of all monsters within earshot. The Grimpet will resist attempts to prise it off, and requires surgical attention.
stats.combat_note: Stat line not present on these pages — the Grimpet header and its full stat block appear on the next page (PDF 203 / printed 196); only the name, type 'Synthetic', and ATK Latch are partially printed here, with descriptive text. LVL/HP/AV/ML/ENC not visible in this range.

special: A larger, more powerful cousin of the Grimpet. Grimweavers were created as sentinels for ancient sites. They spit a nanofibre web that can ensnare even the strongest of creatures, immobilising an intruder and draining their strength. Grimweavers will not pursue beyond the boundaries of the ruin they guard.
Entangled: an Entangled creature has AV9, and cannot move freely. The target must make a DEX save to break free.
stats.combat_note: Web Shot Entangles (target reduced to AV9, cannot move freely, DEX save to break free) plus d4 STR drain. Accompanied by d10 Grimpets.

special: Slow and witless. Drawn towards light and heat. Only attack to defend themselves.
If left alive they have a 1-in-6 chance per day of gestating into a Fungal Horror (see p.xx).
Reanimated by fungus. Move slowly, like sleepwalkers.
stats.combat_note: Level 0 (1 HP). Only attack to defend; drawn to light and heat.

special: Sinuous parasites with the faces of fanged crones.
Siphon: with each succesful attack on a Biological target, the Hagfluke gains 1 Level (Max 7) and regains HP equal to the damage caused.
stats.combat_note: Siphon: each successful hit on a Biological target gains the Hagfluke 1 Level (max 7) and heals it for damage dealt.

special: Large desert snakes, with colouration on their heads that resembles the makeup worn by sacred fools.
Hysteria: A convulsive laughter-like reaction to the serpent's neurotoxins. Afflicted creatures laugh for d6 hours; they cannot speak until the venom wears off.
stats.combat_note: Venom Spray inflicts Hysteria (CON save): afflicted laugh for d6 hours, cannot speak until venom wears off.

special: The Hegemony's officer caste are famed for their extravagant facial hair, their gaudy epaulettes, and their contempt for weakness.
Legionaries in presence of Centurion use the Centurion's morale score.

entries.description: Hegemony officer caste. Famed for extravagant facial hair, gaudy epaulettes, and contempt for weakness.

special: Bomb Collar: Conscripts who fail Morale checks and flee in view of their Ordinator are detonated, dealing 2d6 blast damage to all in melee range. Conscripts without an Ordinator always surrender or flee.
stats.combat_note: The Hegemon's penal battalions are the only mercy the thief or forger can expect. Far from well-trained or equipped, but there is tactical value in every warm body. Minefields, vaults, and other hazardous environments are first explored by conscripts.

attacks.name: Grenade
attacks.damage: d10 blast, DEX save to throw back

special: Reinforcements: If outnumbered, Legionaries fire a distress flare, summoning another d8 Legionaries.
stats.combat_note: Resourceful true-kin soldiers, clad in red armour. The backbone of the Hegemon's occupying forces in Vaarn. Legionaries in presence of Centurion use the Centurion's morale score.

entries.description: Resourceful true-kin soldiers in red armour. Backbone of the Hegemon's occupying forces in Vaarn.

attacks.name: Concussion Grenade
attacks.damage: Blast, d4 DEX damage, DEX save to throw back

special: Battle Trance: Myrmidons enter a hypnotic dream-state before an engagement, which renders their fear instinct obsolete. They will never break in combat, nor will they surrender an inch of ground during their grinding assaults.
stats.combat_note: Siegebreakers, shock troopers, the Hegemon's Hammer. Used against fortified positions or to contain heavily armed foes. A small, elite unit, recognisable by their black ferroplate armour and ritual facial scars.

special: Vitality Sensor: alert on Ordinator death. In Hegemony territory, reinforcements arrive in d10 combat rounds. Contested territory or deep desert: d100 hours.
stats.combat_note: The Hegemony's officer caste are famed for their extravagant facial hair, their gaudy epaulettes, and their contempt for weakness. Legionaries in presence of Centurion use the Centurion's morale score.

attacks.name: Smoke Grenade
attacks.damage: Blast, Blindness, DEX save to throw back

special: Skiff: A squad has one Skiff (p.xx) for each Ranger.
Blindness: Characters blinded by smoke make melee attacks with DIS. They cannot use ranged weapons.
stats.combat_note: The vanguard of the Hegemon's Legions in Vaarn. They eschew the scarlet uniforms of their peers, instead dressing in the blue robes favoured by Faa nomads. Trained in desert survival and sandworm husbandry, and speak the Faa tongue fluently. Operate far from Hegemony bases, spending months in the deep deserts.

attacks.name: Suppression Rifle
attacks.damage: d12 vs all exposed targets, one turn to spin up

attacks.name: Acid Grenade
attacks.damage: d4, Acidic, Blast, DEX save to throw back

special: Stay in rear, laying covering fire.
stats.combat_note: The backbone of a Legionary assault. Suppressors stay in the rear of a Hegemony unit, laying down withering covering fire while their comrades advance or retreat.

special: Assassination technique involves bombing targets' homes with ancient grenades.
stats.combat_note: HP derived as LVL x4 (book printed no explicit HP).

special: The angry bees deal d6 unblockable damage per round to everyone in reach.
stats.combat_note: Human corpses that have been infested by fearsome colonies of Sable Bees. They crawl across the sands, their bellies swollen with a throbbing hive structure.

attacks.name: Grab
attacks.damage: d6 CON damage, STR save to break free

special: Embrace grabbed victims and pull them into the hypergeometric rift in their bodies. While inside, the victim takes d6 CON damage per round as their body dissolves. Must make STR save to pull themselves out.
Unreal Flesh: Hollow Maidens ignore all even-numbered damage rolls.

resistances.notes: Unreal Flesh: ignores all even-numbered damage rolls (stat-block special ability).

stats.combat_note: Spectral women in elegant attire, with wounds in their chests that bleed un-Urthly colours.

special: Well-equipped and trained, but not as numerous as the Legionaries or the Baron's militiamen.
stats.combat_note: HP derived as LVL x4 (book printed no explicit HP).

special: Obeys the wearer of a Dominion Ring without question. Mute, obedient, fearless.
stats.combat_note: An indigo-robed corpse, re-animated by the necrotech implants of the College of Indigo Tigers.

special: Carnivorous species of sandworm. Ambushes from below sand. Sharp, armoured head resembles the ram mounted on the prow of an ancient warship.
stats.combat_note: Per adventure room text (9-Worm Corral): kept unfed for weeks, will attack anything stepping onto the sand; pursues prey onto solid ground but moves much slower when exposed.

attacks.name: Corpse shuck
attacks.damage: takes one round, instant death when target at 0 HP

special: Corpse shuck: Iridium Vultures fanatically attack biological PCs who fall to 0 HP, attempting to break their bodies open and drain out the innards. This lethal attack takes a whole combat round to execute, and can be interrupted by damaging the Vulture or knocking it off balance.
stats.combat_note: Silvery synthetic carrion eaters that ride the air currents above the blue sands, scent-sensors attuned for the slightest hint of decay. Not interested in living beings, but will attack to defend a carcass.

special: Boxy trundling cleaning synth.
Will attempt to dispose of any dead bodies within the facility and take them to the incinerator.
Cannot speak, uninterested in living beings.
stats.combat_note: Attack listed as n/a; non-combatant.

special: Towering, heavily-muscled cannibal. One cunning 'old' head and one foolish new one, created by grafting the head of an elderly clone onto a fresh Weekling.
Begrudgingly subservient towards Mimir; each believes they are the 'true' Autarch.
Styles himself 'Autarch' and will fly into a rage if not addressed as such.
Eats only the flesh of Weeklings.
Carries the Red Keycard and would die before giving it up.
Able to pass through the Laser Hallways without triggering the trap, and will use this to escape from battles that have gone poorly.
stats.combat_note: Physically strong and aggressive; attacks with Dogsbody support, attempts to capture PCs alive for meat.

special: Bearer of a figment of the Jigsaw Autarch. See d4 Autarch Figment table for the effects of the figment.
Autarch Figment (d4): 1 EYE - Bearer's eye becomes a hole of infinite depth. Bearer can cry lances of paradox energy (d10, beam, hypergeometric). Bearer gains the Hypergeometric creature type.

Autarch Figment (d4): 2 GUT - Bearer cradles the Autarch's paradoxical gut inside their body, boosting their resilience. Bearer gains +3 AV and +1 Level. Bearer gains the Hypergeometric creature type.

Autarch Figment (d4): 3 MAW - Bearer's flesh blossoms into a mouth of the Jigsaw Autarch. At close range they make an additional bite attack every round (d10, hypergeometric). Bearer gains the Hypergeometric creature type.

Autarch Figment (d4): 4 NERVES - Bearer's nerves are intertwined with the otherworldly neurons of the Jigsaw Autarch. Bearer gains +1 to INT, PSY and EGO. Bearer may extrude the Autarch's nerves to entangle an opponent (DEX Save vs -5 AV). Bearer gains the Hypergeometric creature type.
stats.combat_note: Stats vary by rolled Autarch Figment (e.g. +3 AV / +1 Level on a GUT result).

entries.description: Bearer of a figment of the Jigsaw Autarch. Conceals true nature under bandages and veils.

special: Bifurcating Bite: the Hoss's bite deals damage equal to half the target's current HP (minimum of 1 damage).

Two Are One: the Jollyhoss's Head and Hindquarters move and attack as two separate Level 4 creatures, each with 16 HP. If one half of the Jollyhoss is killed, it will resurrect with full HP at the start of the next combat round. Only the swift death of the companion half can prevent this.
stats.combat_note: A bizarre hypergeometric predator, which resembles a fanged stallion fashioned from brightly-coloured paper. Comprised of front- and back-halves which move independently, but nonetheless are proven to be the same animal.

special: Notes: Colossal sentient spinning wheel of ferrosteel, which rumbles through the blue wastelands bellowing resonant hymns of loneliness. What it sees it covets, but lacking limbs the Juggernaut can only express affection by attempting to crush the object of its desire, and in so doing make them one with its ever-roving axis.

Kalotoxin: targets stung by the Kalopede's quicksilver tongue must CON Save or undergo rapid transformations into works of Fine Art (p.xx) which vaguely resemble the victim. This metamorphosis is lethal and permanent.
stats.combat_note: A large and hauntingly beautiful centipede-like creature, noted for its polychrome carapace and voracious appetite for fine art objects. Rarely seen on the surface.

entries.description: A large and hauntingly beautiful centipede-like creature with a polychrome carapace. Voracious appetite for fine art. Rarely seen on the surface.

special: A synthetic hound, programmed to display suicidal loyalty to its owner. Pants to cool its Ego-Engines.
Watchdog Protocol: if a physical attack would kill the Synthhound's owner, it kills the Synthhound instead.
stats.combat_note: HP derived as LVL x4 (book printed no explicit HP).

entries.description: Synthetic hound, suicidally loyal. Pants to cool its Ego-Engines.

special: Steed: Mordicant Knights ride a Destrier (p.xx).
stats.combat_note: Sworn swords of the Church of the Everbleeding Wound (p.xx), armoured in blood-red plasteel and bone-white enamel.

special: Steed: Knights Peregrine ride a steed, usually a Weeping Lizard or Zorse. See p.xx for details.
stats.combat_note: The blue wastelands have no shortage of roaming gallants, whose claim to nobility is tenuous and who own little but the clothes on their back and the weapon they have dedicated their life to mastering. Strangers to most and salvation to some.

special: Borrowed Time: the Kronophage drains years from its victim's past, present, and future. The target loses a Level. They must roll 1d8 and subtract the result from their maximum HP, and subtract three points from their maximum ability defences. The Kronophage gains a Level permanently. PCs reduced below Level 0 by the Kronophage are worse than dead; they never existed at all, and their equipment vanishes with them. Slaying the monster restores all lost time to those it fed upon. PCs regain their lost Levels.
stats.combat_note: Manifold crystals orbit a nucleus of collapsing space-time. A paradox made sentient, an ulcer on causality that steals the past from those it beholds.

attacks.name: Blinding Pelt
attacks.damage: Blast, DEX Save vs d6 rounds of Blindness

special: Blindness: PCs blinded make melee attacks with DIS. They cannot use ranged weapons.
stats.combat_note: Lurid cyborg feline. Feeds on sources of electrical power, including synths. Can ignite every filament in its synthetic pelt like a flash-bang.

special: Ruthless planeywoman assassin, dispatched to kill Blotte by a former client he ripped off.
Looks like a cubist painting of a gaunt, battle-scarred woman wearing white.
Fights by pulling out her hair and throwing it at her victims; the 2D filaments slice through armour and flesh like cheese-wire.
Arrives six hours after Blotte and Thunder, aboard a seemingly-empty skiff.
stats.combat_note: Hair Strand resolves against AV 10 regardless of target's actual AV (armour-piercing).

special: Accompanied by d8 Lictors at all hours of the day.
Lonrot is a competent enough duelist, but will not have any interest in risking his life in battle.
If cornered he will use the active camouflage rig inside his robes to become invisible and attempt to escape.
stats.combat_note: Faction leader (Hegemony Consul).

special: Cheap expendable sentries.
stats.combat_note: Shrimp-like synths that fire lasers from their claws. Once used as cheap, expendable sentries.

special: Resurrection: Lazarus Guards will resurrect after d3 combat rounds if slain, the black cyborg hearts within their breasts unwilling to let their hosts die. These hearts must be cut from the guard's body and destroyed in order to stop the resurrection. Once the secret is known, players may wish to target the guard's heart directly. The cyborg organ has 1 HP and AV 20.
stats.combat_note: A desiccated human corpse, filled with necrotech implants that preserve a sort of life-in-death for the unlucky host. So-called 'Lazarus Regiments' were created from the corpses of criminals to guard the tombs of Autarchy nobles. Veins of black gallium pulse beneath parchment-like skin, and their despairing eyes resemble sable stones.

special: Sinuous ambush predators. The worm's gluey spit is highly adhesive; when covered in spit all physical Saves and attack rolls have DIS. The spit is dissolved by salt water.
stats.combat_note: Sinuous ambush predators.

special: Will attempt to reason with their assailants, even during deadly combat.
stats.combat_note: Wandering scholar from the Lithic Lyceum. Generally pacifists, and have little desire to harm living beings.

entries.description: Wandering scholar from the Lithic Lyceum.

attacks.name: Lithifying Ray
attacks.damage: d8 DEX Damage, turn to stone at 0 DEX

special: When the Lyceum has need of defense, it calls upon its rarely seen warrior-scholars. They fight to preserve rather than kill, their defeated foes carefully catalogued in the depths of the Inspiral Archive.
stats.combat_note: Lithifying Ray deals DEX damage; target turns to stone at 0 DEX.

entries.description: Rarely seen warrior-scholars of the Lithic Lyceum. Fight to preserve rather than kill, cataloguing defeated foes in the Inspiral Archive.

special: Will only attack to consume stone.
stats.combat_note: Passive unless consuming stone; appears as d6 in encounter table and 4 in Ballast Stomach Major.

special: The ancients delighted in making pets of all Urth's inhabitants. The Little Torino is a toy species of rhino, roughly the size of a french bulldog.
stats.combat_note: HP derived as LVL x4 (book printed no explicit HP).

entries.description: Toy species of rhino, roughly the size of a french bulldog. Ancient pet-breeding.

special: Frill-necked reptile. Ill-tempered, territorial. Skin prized for boots.
stats.combat_note: Frill-necked reptiles. Ill-tempered, territorial, like a crocodile that can sprint. Their skin is highly prized as a material for boots.

special: If both of Jak's claws hit the same target, she will follow up with a bite attack that deals 2d6 damage, with no to-hit roll required.
She will deal another automatic 2d6 damage to the target she has grabbed each turn, unless they pass a STR save to wrestle her off.
stats.combat_note: Faction leader (Friends of Jak). Alzabo: extra-solar predator that retains the memories of the humans it devours.

special: A nocturnal insect, enraged by artificial light. Relentlessly attacks any lantern or torch-bearing hand it comes across.
stats.combat_note: Sometimes called 'helldiver bugs', due to their ill-fated penchant for assaulting the embers of a campfire.

special: Magnetic Field: the Magneticrab's shell can emit a powerful magnetic field. Each round, nearby PCs with metal weapons or items equipped must STR Save or lose hold of their items. They become stuck to the Magneticrab's shell and cannot be retrieved until the creature is dead. Additionally, PCs wearing metal armour or who are Synthetic are forcibly drawn into melee range.
stats.combat_note: A strange crustacean-like synth, which dwells inside a magnetised shell. The creature emits strong magnetic fields in order to prey upon other synths.

attacks.name: Lash
attacks.damage: d8 + CON save vs Nanomachine Infection

special: Infection: anyone damaged by a Maladaptor's attack must CON save or be infected with malignant nanomachines (p.xx). As these beings are host to numerous infections, the Referee should roll 1d6 to determine what infection has been transmitted: 1 The Gitch, 2 Golden cough, 3 Fabricator Stoma, 4 Usurper Arm, 5 Dreamcage, 6 Janus Lenses.
stats.combat_note: Formed from the broken husks of synths, reanimated by malignant swarms of nanomachines. Move erratically through the blue ruins, seeking fresh hosts for their infestations. A subsonic dirge heralds their approach.

attacks.name: Telekinesis
attacks.damage: 2d8, STR save vs lifted and thrown

special: Prescience: Eyeless Masters telepathically predict the assaults of their opponents, always moving ahead of the blow. They cannot be harmed with any attack unless the attacker learns to shield their intentions, achieved with an opposed PSY Save. Stripped of their prescience, Eyeless Masters have AV 11.

resistances.notes: AV listed as Special. Prescience: cannot be harmed by any attack unless attacker shields intentions via an opposed PSY Save; stripped of prescience, AV becomes 11.

stats.combat_note: Masters of the Eyeless Path, who achieved endarkenment and now guide lesser minds upon the road. Self-blinded and legless, they levitate above the azure dust, resembling emaciated puppets that hang from unseen strings.

special: Symbiotic creatures that aided in the filtration of the Grandfather's ingested sand.
Slowly dying but remain vital.
Grasp moving objects and identify them; biological or metallic objects are carried towards the Metal Stomach, minerals towards the Ballast Stomach Minor.
Resisting the Megacilia requires an opposed STR save.

resistances.notes: Stat block uses 'HD 10' rather than a Level value; recorded HD in raw_excerpt. Morale printed as '15' (no sign).

stats.combat_note: Stat line gives HD 10 (not Level); nonlethal grasp lists no damage value. Morale shown as 15.

special: Biomechanical memory vampire. Like a giant mosquito of living steel.
stats.combat_note: Biomechanical memory vampire. Like a giant mosquito cast from living steel.

attacks.name: 2x Metamorphic Pseudopod
attacks.damage: d4 CON damage, Bio targets CON Save vs mutation

special: A protean mass of primal slurry, in which the stuff of life is devoured and recast. The sludge's digestive enzymes induce rapid mutation in the cells they bond with.
Commands a group of militiamen; will always be found guarding a public fountain.
stats.combat_note: HP derived as LVL x4 (book printed no explicit HP).

special: A severed head, with the features and voice of Rappash-Ik. Suspended in a vat of biotic gel. Moves on slender mechanical limbs.
Believes himself to be the actual head of Rappash-Ik (untrue); is the experiment of a previous Autarch clone.
Master of the Fount; has extended his lifespan by preserving himself in his contraption.
Must recharge his tank in his Laboratory once per day or become immobilised and perish.
Carries the Purple Keycard and would die before giving it up.
No match for the PCs in combat; will seek to bargain, outwit, and use the Fount's traps against them.
stats.combat_note: Avoids direct combat; bargains, flees to control room, sends Janus and Dogsbodies.

special: Sun Scourged: Moonbeasts suffer d10 damage per round if exposed to Urth's red sunlight.

resistances.notes: Sun Scourged: suffers d10 damage per round if exposed to Urth's red sunlight (environmental weakness stated in stat block).

stats.combat_note: Squamous pallid monstrosities from Luna. Inimical to humanity, hated interlopers that dwell in flooded caverns below Luna's surface. Somewhat like a toad and somewhat like an insect. Descend to Vaarn on moonless nights in search of victims, travelling in void-boats made from black stone.

attacks.name: Vampiric Tendrils
attacks.damage: d8, heals HP equal to damage

special: Sun Scourged: Moonbeasts suffer d10 damage per round if exposed to Urth's red sunlight.

resistances.notes: Sun Scourged: suffers d10 damage per round if exposed to Urth's red sunlight (environmental weakness stated in stat block).

stats.combat_note: The immature form of a Moonbeast. Lacking psychic powers or the projectile vomiting of their parents, they instead swarm over their prey and drain the life from their bodies with questing tendrils.

special: Most mycomorphic fungal strains were designed to resurrect human cadavers only, and are incompatible with other species. However, a rare substrain exclusively reanimates canine corpses.
Spores: after each spore attack, the Mycomastiff must CON Save. On failure, no more spores can be expelled without a Long Rest.
stats.combat_note: Spores damage tagged TOX in source (mapped to poison).

entries.description: Rare mycomorphic substrain that exclusively reanimates canine corpses.

special: Human corpses, reanimated by mycomorphic fungal spores. They name themselves the 'twice-born' and can be found throughout Vaarn.
Notes: The mystics of Vaarn hail from many sects.
Mystic Gift: each Mystic is the master of a Gift, which should be generated randomly from the tables on p.xx. The Mystic may teach this Gift to students who appease them.

Opposite Day: Negativfolk always do the opposite of what you ask them, and make every action in reverse. They eject un-chewed food back onto empty plates, blue negativ blood flows back into their wounds. They react poorly to compliments, hugging or shaking the hand of their foes with lethal results. Hurling abuse at a Negativ man may earn you a healing bullet between the eyes. Negativfolk can only be harmed with healing items, and will be healed by damage.

resistances.notes: Opposite Day: can only be harmed with healing items, and will be HEALED by damage (stat-block special). Knife attack listed as '+d6 HP' (heals target).

stats.combat_note: Inverted, photonegative-hued people who walk and speak backwards. They wander the blue dunes in family groups, receding from their point of origin in strange halting meanders.

special: A sentient plant, which enjoys the rights and privileges of any other ensouled citizen of Vaarn.
stats.combat_note: Level listed as 'LVL d6' (variable, rolled); HP not stated as a fixed value.

special: Neural Hijack: hijacked targets must make an opposed EGO save. On failure, the Nerve Crawler bonds with them and is able to direct their actions. The victim may attempt a new EGO save each round to break free.

The formless musicians who attend to the Daemon Sultan Azathoth in the dreaming chaos at the terminus of space and time. The Children summon these pipers and flautists into our reality to aid their rituals.
Sleep: targets fall into a nightmare-wracked sleep and cannot act. They can be woken by direct damage, or anything else that would wake a sleeper.
Feast of Dreams: at the start of the round, a Nightmare Herald regenerates d6 HP for each sleeping creature nearby, allied or enemy. This effect can resurrect the Herald from apparent 'death'.
stats.combat_note: Feast of Dreams regenerates d6 HP per nearby sleeper and can resurrect the Herald from apparent death.

entries.description: Formless musicians attending Azathoth in the dreaming chaos at the terminus of space and time. Summoned by the Children to aid rituals.

special: Vanish: a Nome can disappear inside its cap as a combat action, doubling its AV. The cap sticks to the floor like a limpet, and is impossible to move. While inside the cap the Nome regains all HP.

Summoning Triangle: a group of three Nomes can remove their caps to create a summoning triangle. A single target the Nomes can see must PSY Save or be transported to the centre of the summoning triangle.
stats.combat_note: AV 12 normal, 24 when incapped (vanished into cap). Stat block notation: AV12(24 incap).

special: Nyxia cannot be injured by regular weapons or by Mystic Gifts. Only hypergeometric weapons have any hope of harming her.
She attacks by latching onto an opponent and draining the energy from their body. When their CON is reduced to 0, they are dead.

resistances.notes: Stat block states: cannot be injured by regular weapons or by Mystic Gifts; only hypergeometric weapons have any hope of harming her. This is a stated invulnerability to all non-hypergeometric weapons and to Mystic Gifts.

stats.combat_note: Faction leader (Crimson Court). Planeywoman / hypergeometric being. Freezing Touch deals d8 CON damage; CON to 0 = death.

attacks.name: Oblivion
attacks.damage: 1 EGO damage per round, affects all in line of sight

special: The very sight of the edifice erodes the mind's fabric, replacing the striving will with a terrible blankness.

Oblivion Heralds: unfortunates who have fallen victim to the Obelisk. They seek not to kill but to restrain, forcing captives to kneel unblinking before the black stone until their own mind has been erased. Stats as Bandits (p.xx), but armed with non-lethal weapons.
stats.combat_note: Morale dash (no morale). Comes with d8 Oblivion Heralds (Bandit stats, non-lethal weapons).

special: Lithifying Gaze: automatically hits a target in line of sight. Target loses d6 DEX and gains +2 AV per round; must break line of sight to stop the attack. Both effects fade at the rate of one point per day. An Occulith is immune to its own gaze.
Surprise: the Occulith appears to be inanimate stone until it moves, and always surprises unless the PCs are informed of its exact location.

resistances.notes: Immune to its own gaze (Lithifying Gaze) only.

stats.combat_note: Always surprises unless PCs know its exact location.

special: Plated egg-eating beetles. Aggressive and stupid.
Fanatically attack anything egg-shaped.

attacks.name: Snare
attacks.damage: d6, followed by drowning (STR save vs d6 damage per round)

special: A giant, carnivorous plant that lurks in pools and oases. The Snare hunts by grabbing animals while they drink and dragging them to the bottom of the lake or river, there to be drowned and absorbed into the Snare's root structure.
stats.combat_note: Morale dash (no morale).

attacks.name: Thrown
attacks.damage: d4 (may be thrown; innocent of violence)

special: A humble bluestone of Vaarn, granted sentience and mobility by powers unknown. It rolls after its master in the manner of some lithic supplicant, eager to help however it can. It cannot make a sound but will warn of danger by bumping politely into one's shin.
Living Stone: the Pet Rock does not need to eat, drink, or breathe. It cannot regain HP by any means.

resistances.notes: Cannot regain HP by any means (Living Stone) — not a damage-type resistance.

stats.combat_note: Attack line reads: 'The Pet Rock is innocent of violence but may be thrown for d4 damage.'

entries.description: Humble blue Vaarnish stone, sentient and mobile by powers unknown. Cannot make sound; warns by bumping into shins.

attacks.name: Pounce
attacks.damage: DEX Save vs 2d6 damage per round

special: Phase: At the start of each combat round, the Phase Panther may choose to phase out of reality. While phased, the panther can be seen but cannot be touched or damaged; it likewise cannot touch or harm any non-phased creature.

Pounce: Targets make an opposed DEX save; on failure the target is pinned and takes 2d6 damage per round. While pinned the Panther and target phase out of reality. The target must DEX save to break free and return to the material world.

resistances.notes: Cannot be damaged while phased (Phase ability), but this is a conditional state, not a damage-type resistance.

stats.combat_note: Claws deal hypergeometric damage.

special: Cautious, clever, cerulean-coated pack hunters. Will always flee battle if they are outnumbered.
stats.combat_note: Always flees if outnumbered.

attacks.name: Flense
attacks.damage: d4 ongoing, DEX Save to pull off

special: Burrower: the Moles can burrow in soft ground, doubling their AV.
stats.combat_note: AV 11 normal, 22 when burrowing. Stat block notation: AV11(22).

special: Hypergeometric humans that only have two dimensions.

Flat: Planeyfolk take double damage from slashing or slicing weapons. When encountered, they may be pretending to be wall frescoes or shadows. Make a PSY Save to identify them as living creatures. On failure, they may attack from ambush.
stats.combat_note: Mimic wall frescoes/shadows; PSY Save to identify or they ambush.

special: Aggressive carnivorous beetles. Their heads are thickly armoured and almost impervious to harm, but their abdomens are soft and exposed, with AV 10. They are vulnerable after a charge.

resistances.notes: Head AV 20, abdomen AV 10 (soft/exposed). Vulnerable after a charge. Stat block notation: AV20(10).

stats.combat_note: AV 20 (head/front) vs AV 10 (soft abdomen). Vulnerable after charging.

special: A large venomous arachnid. Named for its colouring, which resembles the red armour worn by the battle-crazed Pontiffs of the Church of the Everbleeding Wound.
stats.combat_note: Sting deals poison damage (TOX -> poison).

special: Carry doses of Summerbalm (heals for d8 HP).
stats.combat_note: HP derived as LVL x4 (book printed no explicit HP).

special: If combat breaks out, the referee should roll to determine which drug Prieval is high on.
Even numbers designate amphetamines; Prieval is twitchy and fast, and acts twice before the PCs do. However, he will bug out and run as soon as the fight goes against him.
Odd numbers designate opiates; Prieval is disassociating and will always attack last. However, he has no concept of the danger he is in, cannot feel pain, and will never run away.
stats.combat_note: Faction leader (Prieval's Crew). Morale is 'See Below' (drug-dependent behaviour, not a numeric value).

special: Severely mutated humans that resemble enormous ambulatory torsos. They have a primitive, furious face on their chest, and tiny vestigial arms. They are unintelligent but ferocious and will pursue prey for miles.

A flightless blue owl with delicate pink eyes. Psy-Owls mentally dominate small animals and force them to climb into the owl's beak. Larger creatures that fall under the Owl's influence are tasked with capturing small lizards and desert mice and hand-feeding them to the gluttonous bird.

attacks.name: Psyche Syphon
attacks.damage: grab, d6 PSY damage per round, STR save to break free

special: What appears to be a man is merely the beast's shell: from within the ambling corpse's skull blooms a ravenous tangle of questing tendrils. The otherworldly leech is drawn to the brains of active psychics.
Gleam Seeker: PCs with Gleam (p.xx) are always visible to the Leech, regardless of distance. They cannot surprise the creature.
Immunity: the Leech is immune to damage caused by Mystic Gifts.

resistances.notes: Immune to damage caused by Mystic Gifts.

stats.combat_note: Cannot be surprised by PCs with Gleam. Immune to Mystic Gift damage.

attacks.name: Generate two Daemon Attacks (see Daemon Attack table, printed p.234)

special: Level: 3d6
Morale: +2d6
A mighty Quantum Daemon, whose paradoxical footprint upon our reality is trampling and impetuous.
Incorporeal: the Daemon does not actually exist, and cannot be harmed nor harm others unless it is forced to manifest itself.
Daemon Abilities: generate two special Daemon Abilities (see Daemon Ability table, printed p.234).

resistances.notes: No FIXED resistances printed in the stat block. The Daemon is Incorporeal (cannot be harmed unless forced to manifest). Any immunities come from the rolled Daemon Ability table (printed p.234), of which a Greater Daemon generates two; these vary per individual. Possible rolled immunity-type abilities include Immune to Fire, Immune to Cold, Immune to Poison and Fungal Spores, Immune to Electrical Weapons, Immune to Beam Weapons, Immune to Physical Damage, Immune to All Damage (Harmed by Healing), Immune to Mystic Gifts and Hypergeometry, Immortal Unless True Name Spoken. NOT fixed for this creature.

stats.combat_note: Killing a Quantum Daemon is not possible with conventional weaponry, as they do not actually exist.
